placeholders.${broker}: the broker's base URL, with no trailing slash
placeholders.${token_endpoint}: ${broker} with token_endpoint_path appended: the htu every proof names
placeholders.${subject_token}: the subject token the client's source answered for this exchange
placeholders.${actor_token}: the machine's own Google identity token, for the one exchange that carries an actor
placeholders.${session}: the session name the caller asks to write under

never_sent.audience: RFC 8693's audience names the service a token is asked for. This exchange mints the broker's own access token and nothing else, so the broker reads no audience, and a client that sends one sends a field the other client does not.
never_sent.requested_token_type: The exchange mints an access token and only an access token, so the default is the only answer and naming it adds a field the two clients could disagree on.
never_sent.scope: The broker grants the scope the entry decides; a scope in the form is neither read nor honoured.
never_sent.client_secret: The exchange client is registered confidential but presents no credential of its own: the subject token and the proof of the caller's key are what the broker judges the request on.

dpop.nonce: A proof carries a nonce claim only after the broker has answered 400 use_dpop_nonce with a DPoP-Nonce header, and then that nonce and no other; the first proof of a request carries none.
dpop.ath: A token endpoint request presents no access token, so its proof carries no ath.

fields.access_token: the broker's opaque access token, bound to the key the proof presented
fields.expires_in: seconds the access token lives, an hour or less

optional_fields.credential_id: the launcher credential the trade minted or re-used, which a caller that enrols sessions needs and a caller that only writes to Dispatch ignores

forbidden_fields.refresh_token: This grant issues none: a renewal is a fresh subject token traded again. A client that kept one would keep a credential the broker never minted, so an answer carrying one is refused.

refuse.name: the broker refuses the subject token

body.error_description: the machine example-machine@example.iam.gserviceaccount.example is in no fleet this broker lists

refuse.client: stops with a plain error carrying the broker's error and error_description, holds no token, and writes nothing

refuse.name: the answer carries a refresh token
refuse.client: refuses the answer naming refresh_token: this grant issues none, and no client of it ever keeps one

refuse.name: the answer names no access token

exchanges.name: kubernetes-projected
exchanges.what: A pod trades the projected service-account token its runtime mounts, read again from its file before every trade.

exchanges.name: google-machine
exchanges.what: A machine trades its own Google identity token: the one its Compute Engine metadata server mints, or one minted for it through a workload identity pool.

exchanges.name: person-sign-in
exchanges.what: A person who signed in on a machine trades their own Google identity token with that machine's as the actor token (RFC 8693 section 2.1), proving the box key the sign-in is bound to.

exchanges.name: access-token
exchanges.what: A session on a dev box trades the access token its machine login holds for one of its own.
